Solutions 1 and 2 give the same answer, $p^n+p-1$, from the orders $p-1$, $p^{n-1}$, and $p^{n-1}(p-1)$. Those three orders are distinct for odd $p$ and $n \ge 2$, and the arithmetic checks out. Solution 3's reasoning is unsupported: it asserts the classification without justification and picks subgroups of index 2 and $p$ with no argument. I could not verify the classification of the three subgroups from memory, so Solutions 1 and 2 are the best-supported answers, but this is not a full verification. Solution 1 is listed first, so I select it.

CHOICE: 1
